newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India cautious, Taiwan awaits Deng news.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India cautious, Taiwan awaits Deng news.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts moved lower on Tuesday to what brokers said were more "realistic levels" in a day of selective trade.
"The premiums of GDRs are now down to more normal levels of 13-14 pct," said broker Deepak Lalwani of Astaire & Partners.
The indicative Cazenove Indian GDR index closed 1.39 points or 1.75 percent lower at 77.95.
Traders said demand was restricted to blue chip shares, mainly Indian Hotels, Steel Authority of India Ltd and vehicle maker Mahindra & Mahindra.
They said there was some demand from Bombay traders and from the Far East.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 50.06 points to 3,530.23. Traders in London said they expected prices to be on the lower side before India's central budget on February 28.
"We are waiting for more (economic) reforms," one trader said.
The Capel Indian GDR index lost 1.39 points or 1.94 percent at 70.22.
The Capel Taiwanese GDR index fell 0.47 points or 0.46 percent at 101.56 with traders anticpating more firm news on the Chinese leader Deng Xiaping.
"All attention is on Beijing," a dealer said.
Press reports quoting sources said on Monday that Deng's deteriorating health had forced Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin and other leaders to cut short provincial trips to the capital.
"Demand was mostly restricted to hi-tech companies," a trader said.
Acer Inc 2306.Q showed resilience by edging ahead by 0.25 cents to $11.05 in a market which maintained a weak undertone.
China Steel 2002.Q came under selling pressure as it lost 0.32 cents to $18.375.
Korean prices remained mostly firm with the Capel Korea index inching ahead by 0.28 points or 0.43 percent to 64.59 as it reflected a 42.20 percent premium over local prices.
